citations.claim: total energy at step 3 exceeds allowed limit, the first violation
initial total energy before bounce and fall
outgoing speed after ceiling bounce already exceeds incoming speed
energy grows monotonically during free fall after bounce showing integrator injection

counterfactual.change: Set gravity 9.81 to 0, keeping all else identical; bounce alone then conserves energy exactly so violation disappears, implicating gravity integration / gravity-bounce interaction.

explanation: Single ball launched upward at ~41.4 m/s from y=11.6 hits arena ceiling within step 1 and bounces elastically (e=1). With gravity=0 the same bounce conserves energy exactly, but with gravity=9.81 total energy grows every step after the bounce (972->973->1031->1092 J) while controller_work=0. Outgoing speed exceeds incoming (40.47 up to 40.73 down magnitude) and keeps growing. Likely cause: gravity velocity update combined with substepped semi-implicit Euler and ceiling impulse/positional correction double-counts gravitational work or adds spurious g*v*dt energy each substep at high speed, so elastic ceiling collision under gravity injects net energy.
vision_note: A single ball starts just below the top wall in step 0 and moves steadily downward through steps 1 to 3. There is no visible penetration, tunneling, or sudden jump, just continuous falling motion after an apparent ceiling contact.
